materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure changes the granularity and specificity of the allocation methodology for shared functional expenses. Previously, the policy was generic (sales/marketing/engineering etc. generally allocated to segments). The 2024 disclosure explicitly states that sales and marketing are allocated only to Intel Products segments, while finance and administration are allocated to all segments except Mobileye. This specificity alters the understanding of how costs are assigned to specific operating segments, particularly regarding the Mobileye segment, which is a material business entity.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Specific allocation of shared expenses by segment and function

comparisons.peer_summary: Direct operating expenses are charged to specific segments, while indirect expenses are allocated based on cost of goods sold or forecasted wafer production. The company does not report assets (other than goodwill), capital expenditures, or certain income/expense items by segment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose methodologies for allocating indirect operating expenses across their operating segments. Intel allocates finance and administration expenses to all segments except Mobileye, while Micron allocates indirect expenses based on cost of goods sold or forecasted wafer production. Intel's approach is function-based (excluding one segment), whereas Micron uses a volume/cost driver metric.

sentences.text: We allocate operating expenses from our sales and marketing group to the Intel Products operating segments and allocate operating expenses from our finance and administration groups to all of our operating segments, except Mobileye.
Certain operating expenses directly associated with the activities of a specific segment are charged to that segment.
Other indirect operating income and expenses are generally allocated to segments based on their respective percentage of cost of goods sold or forecasted wafer production.
